title: Import a DXF drawing and use its profiles as geometry for 2D cuts

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: needs-research
labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on."

What is missing: the importers read solid and mesh models only. A 2D drawing (a DXF from a CAD or sheet-metal program) cannot be loaded, so a flat part cannot be profiled without first being modelled as a solid. No DXF code exists in the tree today; issues 743 and 744 want DXF for tool and fixture profiles and can share this reader.

Wanted:
- A DXF reader for the 2D entities that carry a profile: LINE, ARC, CIRCLE, LWPOLYLINE and POLYLINE (with bulges), ELLIPSE and SPLINE (flattened within a tolerance, arcs kept as arcs where they are arcs). Units from `$INSUNITS`, with a question to the user when the file states none (never a silent guess between mm and inch). Layers are kept, so the user can pick by layer. Blocks/INSERT are expanded or refused by name; text, dimensions and hatches are skipped and counted in the import summary.
- The drawing loads as sketch geometry on the setup's XY plane: shown in the viewport, placed with the stock, saved in the project file.
- Chaining: touching entities are joined into chains within a tolerance; closed chains are told from open ones, and outer loops from holes.
- The 2D operations (2D Contour first; Pocket, Slot, Engrave and the plasma/laser profile operations after) take those chains as their geometry selection, with side (inside/outside) and direction per chain, exactly as they take model edges today.
- Loading is an undoable command with its MCP tool (Everything Is a Command; commands ship with an MCP tool). Model > Open offers `.dxf`, and so does the viewport drop of issue 1450.

Safety:
- The reader is an importer of untrusted files: malformed group codes, truncated files, NaN or huge coordinates, zero-length entities and self-intersecting loops give a clean error or a named skip, never a crash or a hang; it gets a fuzz test like the other importers.
- A gap wider than the chaining tolerance leaves an open chain that is shown as open; it is never closed silently, and an inside/outside cut on an open chain is refused by name.
- A flattened spline or ellipse stays within the stated tolerance of the drawn curve, pinned by a test, so the cut part is to size.
- Units are part of the result: the import summary states them, and a wrong-unit part (25.4 times too big or small) cannot happen without the user having answered the question.

Sources: the DXF format from Autodesk's published DXF reference (a public file-format document; format only), written from scratch or through a permissively licensed crate if one fits (a new dependency needs the maintainer's yes and a `docs/decisions/` entry). No DXF sample files taken from another product's install tree.

Scope note: this is larger than one PR. Suggested split when it is picked up: (1) reader + fuzz test in the geometry crate, (2) sketch entity, project file and viewport display, (3) chaining and selection in 2D Contour, (4) the other 2D operations.

Done means: a DXF with an outer rectangle, two circles and a slot made of lines and arcs loads, shows in the viewport and survives save/reopen; a 2D Contour picks the outer loop (outside) and the holes (inside) and posts a program whose golden CL matches the drawn sizes; a file with no units asks; an open chain is shown and refused for a side-compensated cut; a corrupt DXF gives a named error; the fuzz test runs; undo removes the drawing; the MCP tool loads a DXF headlessly.
